a-poetry-handbook-by-mary-oliver.title: A Poetry Handbook by Mary Oliver
a-poetry-handbook-by-mary-oliver.content:
Thoughts about the Book
It would build trust if you could read her as a poet before you read her as a guide.
At Black River by Mary Oliver
I think this is such a great poem for a couple of clear reasons. On page 65 of the book, Mary Oliver describes a poem called The Fish by Marianne Moore. The form of the poem The Fish uses the exact same syllables in each line, which creates a form that promises something, and then delivers. Mary Oliver doesn’t use the same format - her syllables vary from line to line, but the enjambment of the poem serves the same function - it promises, and delivers, creating pleasure.
Nothing I can say is going to build much on the book, because it’s concise, well thought out, and wise. I keep coming back to it for inspiration when I am running aground, trying to capture something. I think it’s very much worth reading.

metaphors.title: Metaphors
metaphors.content:
If metaphor is the structure of thought rather than a poetic technique, then poetry is not decoration. Poetry is a kind of applied cognitive research. Great poets have always been running experiments on the metaphor system.
Changing the metaphor changes what’s possible.
While all that is probably true, I think there’s a rocky ledge, and there’s probably a gateway through it, so that you don’t scrape your boat too much going through it. The trick is that you might need to bring those metaphors into a more personal, less teacherly space to use those metaphors in a way that can bring about change for yourself and for those who come across whatever metaphor castle you’re trying to build.

No Tomb of His Own: Legacies of the Hollywood Buck
Overview of the book
No Tomb of His Own: Legacies of the Hollywood Buck is a chapbook that looks hand made, creating by a group of poets, editors and artists from Richmond, VA. It was published May 2024.
The Hollywood Cemetary Buck Story
There’s no place where you can read the chapbook online, but here’s a picture of the outside of the book.
Transclude of img_8173.heic
Thoughts
It’s really difficult to weigh in on a work that touched so many people and dealt with such sensitive issues. The cultures that weave through one another in this city sometimes cause fraying in the fabric. There are several hunters who wrote poems for this collection, but they are a minority. I am going to ask for permission to put some of the poems from this chapbook online, and that will help me make better commentary on the work.

river-mouse.title: River Mouse
river-mouse.content:
Something crawls through the long grass
Towards the darkness in my tent
I wake up from fitful dreaming
It goes silent
I lean upwards
Hauling off my sheets
It crawls along the side of the vestibule
That keeps the dew from forming on my face
I kick out at the side of my tent gently
The unseen creature scurries
Into the silence
I close my eyes to fall asleep again
Trying to douse the fire
Of the questions in my head
Giving up worry because
I’ve seen these things before
Then it’s chewing, chewing, chewing
Rustling so near my head
I can’t help but sit bolt upright
Wondering whether I should
Tear out of my tent
Stomp loud enough to scare the creature
Insect, snake, or little mink
Like the ones I saw crossing the road
Coming back from the river
Instead I kick out where I think it might be
In the starlight prickled darkness
A little crescent moonlight diffused
Through the tent cloth
Now I am more awake than I have ever been
I remember I left out a sandwich in a bag
Then the creature is silent, I must have made
My point, it is so quiet for so long,
I decide it’s best to get as much sleep as
A lonely camper can
Then it’s crawling between the netting
Revealing it’s form - a field mouse
The size of my hand above me,
Staring down at me, recusingly
As if it wants to say I left the sandwich
So I should be at peace to let it eat its dinner
Without such rude host manners
It scurries suddenly, above my face
I scootch sideways
In case it finds a way to get much closer
No telepathy between us
Though the bridge of air is small
We star at each other
My heart’s beating fast
But the mouse seems calm
With a flicker of fast movement
Mouse vanishes from sight
It’s quiet for two minutes
Before the cycle begins again
But this time Mouse has a plan
To catch me laying there
Just as soon as I swing out
A slow foot to chase away
He slips underneath my tent floor
Thin fabric and a half full bedroll
Mouse is scurrying underneath my back
Thrill of electric jolt through me
I try to turn and wiggle
But I can’t stay away
I make my move so fast,
Hurtling out of the zippered tent
Then I turn at stare at it
Like the mouse will chase me out
Then I walk away, down the field into the night
Past the other people’s tents
Who I have probably woken up
I walk about two minutes
In the chilly misty night
An unknown hour, a silly throb
Of an unidentified emotion
Then I gather all the things
That I left beside the tent
Except the sandwhich I can’t see
Because I will not use a light
When I have things arranged
When the car door light dims again
I see across my tent
That the other zipper is ajar

river-poem-no.-1.title: River Poem No. 1
river-poem-no.-1.content:
Reddish quiet sand between the stones
sweep like letters scrolling down the river
but I flow on the current too close to
be literate or remember what it says
long locks of green grasses stare me
down tips gliding through the surface
vees ripple from each tip like letters
but I flow on the surface too close to
let the memories flood my mind
patterns flocking little waves moving in lock
step crossed by manic motion of subtle smaller
flocks of lines of tiny currents in
the square foot my eyes are locked on
without the light shattered correctly
over the surface of the thin sheet
I would never see it
or have it written inside me
it is happening now the writing
of the river flowing and cascading falling
into the sounds of sunset
but i cannot see it and i never will remember
until i float again still too close to read

sail-making.title: Sail Making
sail-making.content:
The time it takes to make the cloth
To twist the rope, and press the oakum in
The wind is worth the catching
The breeze is laughing, rising fast
Into a sky the blue of days
The tone of bells down the hallway
Make peace, make art, make love
On teak, mahogany, and oak
Whitewash the stars and bless
The wake of clouds that skein
The dark behind the sky
Pull back your hair and balance
Easy while time take it easy
Your bones relax, your scars
Forget their song and salty
Wind taunts the catch
If this combination
Of wind and sun and water
Inebriates some truths
Mom knew that the drug was worth the taking
